info.title: Everserve operator API
info.description: Engines, nodes and pools, each a spec and a status. Every request is authenticated and authorized (decision 0039); the objects, their versions, watches and errors are decision 0042's.

get.summary: List the engines, or watch them.

parameters.name: watch
parameters.description: Stream changes, one JSON line each, rather than list.

parameters.name: resourceVersion
parameters.description: For a watch: the version to stream from. Absent, every object is sent as `ADDED` first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: For a list: at most this many objects, with a `continue` token when there are more.

parameters.name: continue
parameters.description: For a list: the token the previous page gave, to read the next one.

200.description: Every engine, or with `watch`, its changes as JSON lines

410.description: The watch's version is too old: list again

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The engine's name in the policy

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The engine's name in the policy

post.summary:
Ask a process of an engine for its stacks: a serving rank (or the spare preloaded for it or
taking it), a spare standing for any position by its node and device, or the head.

parameters.name: engine
parameters.description: The engine's name in the policy

502.description: The process's node did not answer

get.summary:
List the nodes, or watch them: every node whose daemon is linked, that has a spec, or that
holds a member of an engine.

parameters.name: watch
parameters.description: Stream changes, one JSON line each, rather than list.

parameters.name: resourceVersion
parameters.description: For a watch: the version to stream from. Absent, every object is sent as `ADDED` first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: For a list: at most this many objects, with a `continue` token when there are more.

parameters.name: continue
parameters.description: For a list: the token the previous page gave, to read the next one.

200.description: Every node, or with `watch`, its changes as JSON lines

410.description: The watch's version is too old: list again

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The node's name

put.summary:
Write a node's spec: cordon it, drain it by a deadline, or withdraw either. What came of it
is the node's status: its Draining condition says whether the drain is `Scheduled` or
`Waiting` its turn.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The node's name

409.description: `Conflict`: the node changed since the version written against; `DrainUnderway`: the write moves or clears a drain whose notices went out

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The node's name

get.summary:
Whether a node may be given back now, and why not; with `wait_ms`, once it may
or when the wait runs out.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The node's name

parameters.name: wait_ms
parameters.description: How long to wait for the node to become releasable, in milliseconds; absent, answer now.

parameters.name: watch
parameters.description: Stream changes, one JSON line each, rather than list.

parameters.name: resourceVersion
parameters.description: For a watch: the version to stream from. Absent, every object is sent as `ADDED` first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: For a list: at most this many objects, with a `continue` token when there are more.

parameters.name: continue
parameters.description: For a list: the token the previous page gave, to read the next one.

200.description: Every pool, or with `watch`, its changes as JSON lines

410.description: The watch's version is too old: list again

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description: The pool's name

put.summary: Write a pool's spec; its launcher is kept as it is.

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description: The pool's name

409.description: The pool changed since the version written against

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description: The pool's name

get.summary: Read how a pool's spares are launched.

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description: The pool's name

put.summary:
Write how a node's daemon launches one of the pool's spares: a command every node of the
pool runs, written under a grant of its own (`update pools/launcher`).

parameters.name: pool
parameters.description: The pool's name

409.description: The pool's spec was written meanwhile: write again

AckStamp.description: An acknowledgement and when its daemon received it, on that daemon's clock.

AnySpareReadiness.description: One spare standing for any position (decision 0030).

oneOf.description: The spare's process, as its node's daemon saw it register.

state.description: `standing` in the pool, or `taking` a rank in the change in flight.

ApiError.description: An error as the operator API answers it.

ChangeReadiness.description: A change in flight: the epoch it claimed and the ranks it takes.

epoch.description: The epoch the change claimed; readiness's `epoch` reaches it at the commit.

CompileCacheReadiness.description: The compiled-kernel cache a process reported running with (decision 0029).

digest.description: The digest over every file under it, the autotune results included.

Condition.description: One condition as status carries it.

lastTransitionMs.description: When its status last changed, Unix milliseconds on the coordinator's clock.

CoverReadiness.description: An engine's cover plan, as readiness shows it (decision 0035).

epoch.description: The committed epoch it is for.

failed.description: Groups a member could not form under it.

uncovered.description: The losses it holds no set for, with why.

CoverSetReadiness.description: One set of a cover plan.

covered.description: Every member of every one of its groups reported it formed.

formed.description: Of those, the ones every member reported.

purpose.description: What it is for: `current`, or the loss it answers and how.

set.description: Its members, joined by `-`: a rank, or `R<rank>@<node>:<device>` for a spare.

class.description: The product name the driver reports; the class a fit compares.

domain.description: The domain it reaches at full speed (the node, until a wider domain is found).

index.description: The index the engine's `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and `Member.device` use.

atMs.description: Since when, Unix milliseconds on the coordinator's clock.

cause.description:
`stopped`, `failed` or `lost` from the head's departure, or `change_failed` when a change
failed after its delivery.

detail.description: The head's goodbye, or the failed change's error.

deadlineMs.description:
When the node goes, Unix milliseconds: a time, never a lead, so the same spec written
twice asks the same thing.

Engine.description:
An engine: its spec is its entry in the policy, read-only here; its status, what a
framework or a scheduler reads before it acts on the engine.

spec.description: Its entry in the policy, in the policy's protobuf JSON.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

EngineReadiness.description: One engine as the scheduler sees it.

anySpares.description:
Spares standing for any position of the engine (decision 0030): they hold the model in host
memory and take the shard of the rank a change names, so REPLACE is available for any rank
while one is in the pool.

oneOf.description: The change in flight, if one is (decision 0032).

compileCacheConsistent.description:
The engine has a key, every serving rank reported it, and every spare in the pool reported
the pair of the rank it stands in for (digests differ by rank on a pipeline engine, since
each stage compiles its own graph). False means a spare's rows would not match its
position's, or a process reported none, so nothing holds it: a scheduler does not run an
exact change on the engine either way.

compileKey.description:
The compile cache key the engine's first registered process reported (decision 0029): one
engine, one compiled artifact, which every later process must report; absent until one
did, and again once every process of the engine has gone, so a re-formed engine sets its
own.

conditions.description:
What its status means (decision 0036): Serving, Progressing, Covered, Degraded and Down,
each with its reason and when it last changed.

oneOf.description:
The cover plan delivered for the engine and how much of it is formed (decision 0035);
absent while cover is not planned.

Why the engine is down and since when (decision 0032); absent while it is not. A down
engine takes no change until its head registers again.

engine.description: The engine's name in the policy.

epoch.description:
The last committed membership epoch. A change in flight shows in `change`, never here:
between a change's claim and its commit the members it takes are gone from `members` and
its spares are not yet in it.

oneOf.description:
The engine's head (decision 0032): the process that owns its scheduler and executor, and
its launcher. Absent until it registered, and while the engine is down.

A second head that registered on another node while the engine's head was alive, refused:
two processes believe they own the engine, which an operator must resolve.
The last committed change's record: what it cost, and where the time went.

lost.description: Ranks lost to SHRINK, still counted against the policy's concurrent losses.

nodes.description: Every node holding a member: whether it can be reclaimed, and how.

refusedSpares.description:
Spares kept out of the pool for what they run (decision 0034), with the field that
differed: a spare an operator expects in the pool and does not find is here.

spares.description: Spares standing behind the engine, each for one rank.

state.description:
The instance's state in a framework's terms (decision 0041): what an integration reports
to the framework that routes to the engine.

Event.description: One event: what the controller decided or saw, and why.

atMs.description: When, Unix milliseconds on the coordinator's clock.

EventType.description: What a watch's event says happened.

FailedGroupReadiness.description: A group a member could not form.

group.description: The members it spans, in rank order: a group is shared by every set that needs it.

HeadReadiness.description: An engine's head as its node's daemon saw it register (decision 0032).

host.description:
The address its engine core registered; empty when it named none. Front ends find the
core through their framework's own discovery; this is for people.

launcherPid.description:
The process the operator launched, as the head reported it in its own pid namespace; the
engine core's own when it runs in that process. For people: nothing is signalled by it.

pid.description:
The engine core's process id, from the daemon socket's peer credentials; absent when the
daemon cannot see it, as a process in another pod on Kubernetes.

registeredAtMs.description: When it registered, Unix milliseconds on the coordinator's clock.

IdentityReadiness.description: What a process runs (decision 0034), as readiness reports it.

adapterDirty.description: Whether the adapter was built from a tree with uncommitted changes.

checkpointDigest.description: The digest over the checkpoint's snapshot.

kvLayoutHash.description: The hash of the KV's layout for the position; empty for a spare standing for any position.

layout.description: The parallel widths: tensor, pipeline, data, expert, context.

quantization.description: The quantization method, empty for none.

InstanceState.description:
An instance's state in a framework's terms (decision 0041's second obligation), derived from
its engine's view in one place, the first that holds.

JoinStamp.description: A join payload through the coordinator.

forwardedAtUs.description: Each node it was forwarded to, and when its forward was queued to that node's link.

fromClient.description: True for the executor's payload to the process, false for the process's answer back.

rank.description: The rank whose position it joins.

receivedAtUs.description: When the coordinator read it from its node's daemon.

LastChange.description:
A committed change's record. Its moments are on the coordinator's clock, microseconds since
the Unix epoch, except each acknowledgement's, which is its daemon's.

acks.description: Every acknowledgement it waited on: which process the change waited for longest.

cover.description:
How it used cover (decision 0035): through which covered set, or formed in the change;
empty while cover is not planned.

deliveredAtUs.description: Its delivery to the survivors and spares.

joins.description:
The join payloads routed for its epoch (decision 0024), at most 64, before or after its
commit: the control plane's share of a take's join and its answers.

Launcher.description:
How a node's daemon starts one of a pool's spares: a command every node of the pool runs,
so writing it is a grant apart from the pool's (`update pools/launcher`).

command.description: The command and its arguments; empty, the daemons launch nothing.

continue.description: The token for the next page of a paged list (`?limit=N`); absent on the last page.

resourceVersion.description:
The version the list was read at: a watch from it misses no change. On every page of a
paged list, the first page's.

List_Engine.description: Every object of a kind, in name order.

items.description:
An engine: its spec is its entry in the policy, read-only here; its status, what a
framework or a scheduler reads before it acts on the engine.

spec.description: Its entry in the policy, in the policy's protobuf JSON.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

List_Node.description: Every object of a kind, in name order.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

List_Pool.description: Every object of a kind, in name order.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

class.description: Its device class, when the node reported devices.

oneOf.description: The compile cache it reported (decision 0029); absent when it reported none.
The process serving the rank, as its node's daemon saw it register.

replicatesTo.description: The replica addresses its store sends every commit to.

generation.description: Raised by each write of its spec; 0 for a spec never written through the API.

name.description: The object's name: the engine's in the policy, the node's, the pool's.

resourceVersion.description:
Raised by any change of the object as the API shows it, spec or status: what a write's
precondition and a watch name. Opaque: `<term>.<n>`, comparable only for equality.

writtenAtMs.description: When its spec was last written, Unix milliseconds; 0 for a spec never written.

writtenBy.description: Who wrote its spec last, as the API authenticated them, or the notice that did.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

NodeEngine.description: One engine's part of a node.

outcome.description: The outcome a loss of the node now would take.

reclaimable.description: Whether a loss of the node now is replaced, not rebuilt.

why.description: Why, when it is not replaced.

NodeReadiness.description: Whether one node can be reclaimed now and what the engine would do.

expectedPauseMs.description:
The last pause this coordinator measured for that outcome on this engine; absent until one
was.

minNoticeMs.description: The shortest notice the policy treats as a notice rather than a fault.

outcome.description: The outcome the policy would take: `replace`, `shrink` or `rebuild`.

reclaimable.description: Losing every rank on it keeps the engine serving.

why.description: Why it is not reclaimable; empty when it is.

NodeRelease.description:
Whether a node may be given back now: it holds no position, nothing is staged
onto or from it, and no change in flight touches it. What maintenance and reclaim tooling asks
before it returns a node, rather than reading conditions and waiting for `DrainDone`.

releasable.description: Whether it may be given back.

why.description: Why not, each reason in words; empty when it may.

NodeSpec.description: A node's spec: what an operator, a cloud's notice or a Node's label asks of it.

oneOf.description:
Drained: every rank on it moved to a spare by the deadline, then the node released. A
drained node is cordoned.

unschedulable.description: Cordoned: no spare takes a position on it; what it holds stays.

NodeStatus.description: What the coordinator observes of a node.

conditions.description:
`Draining` (reason `Scheduled`: its notices went out; `Waiting`: other drains move as
many positions as the policy allows at once; `Blocked`: its change was refused; or
`NotDraining`) and `Degraded` (`DrainBlocked`). A cordon is the spec's `unschedulable`.

devices.description: Its devices, as its daemon reported them.

engines.description: Each engine with ranks on it.

linked.description: Its daemon is linked to the coordinator.

replicaAddress.description: Where its store takes replicas; absent when it takes none.

status.description: What the coordinator observes of it.

PoolSpec.description: A pool's spec (decision 0031). Its launcher is written apart, under a grant of its own.

deviceClass.description: The device class a spare must stand on; empty for any.

domain.description: The network domain a spare must stand in; empty for any.

engines.description: The engines it holds spares for, of one shape.

wants.description: How many spares it wants standing.

PoolStatus.description: What the coordinator observes of a pool.

deficit.description: `wants` less `standing` and `warming`: what its launches, or a scheduler, keep at zero.

standing.description:
Spares standing for any of its engines on an uncordoned node its selector admits, each
process counted once.

taking.description: Spares taking a position in a change in flight.

warming.description: Spares launched for it that have not yet registered.

ProcessReadiness.description:
A process the control plane serves, as its node's daemon saw it register: the id is the
socket's peer credential, never the process's own word.

oneOf.description: What it runs, as it registered (decision 0034); absent when it reported nothing.

pid.description:
The process id on its node; absent when the daemon cannot see it, as a process in another
pod on Kubernetes.

registeredAtMs.description: When it registered, Unix milliseconds on the coordinator's clock.

Reason.description: Why a request was not done, from a closed set a client matches on.

RefusedSpareReadiness.description: A spare kept out of an engine's pool for what it runs (decision 0034).

rank.description: The rank it stood for; absent for a spare standing for any position.

reason.description: Why: the field that differed, or the identity it did not report.

Severity.description: Whether an event is routine or calls for attention.

detail.description: What the probe found, for a human.

oneOf.description: The compile cache it reported (decision 0029); absent when it reported none.
The spare's process, as its node's daemon saw it register.

rank.description: The rank it stands in for.

speed.description: Expected speed relative to the position's class (1.0: the same class).

StacksRequest.description:
What a stacks request names: a serving rank (or the spare preloaded for it or taking it), a
spare standing for any position by its node and device, or the engine's head.

device.description: A spare standing for any position: its device.

head.description: The engine's head, its launcher asked too (decision 0032).

node.description: A spare standing for any position: its node.

StacksTaken.description: A stacks request done: the process asked on its link, on which node, and when.

answered.description:
Whether the process answered with its stacks in time; one that does not writes them to
its own log only.

atMs.description: When the daemon was asked, Unix milliseconds.

pid.description:
The process asked for its stacks; absent when its daemon cannot see its id, as another
pod's on Kubernetes.

stacks.description: Its every thread's stack, as it answered; at most 1 MiB.

UncoveredReadiness.description: A loss a cover plan holds no set for.

object.description: The object as it is after the change; as it was last shown, for a deletion.

WriteMetadata.description: The precondition a write may carry.

resourceVersion.description:
The object's `resourceVersion` as the writer read it: the write is refused, 409
`Conflict`, if the object changed since. Absent, the write applies as it stands.

Write_NodeSpec.description:
A write of an object's spec. An object read and sent back is a valid write: its `status` and
its metadata other than `resourceVersion` are ignored.

spec.description: A node's spec: what an operator, a cloud's notice or a Node's label asks of it.

oneOf.description:
Drained: every rank on it moved to a spare by the deadline, then the node released. A
drained node is cordoned.

unschedulable.description: Cordoned: no spare takes a position on it; what it holds stays.

Write_PoolSpec.description:
A write of an object's spec. An object read and sent back is a valid write: its `status` and
its metadata other than `resourceVersion` are ignored.

spec.description: A pool's spec (decision 0031). Its launcher is written apart, under a grant of its own.

deviceClass.description: The device class a spare must stand on; empty for any.

domain.description: The network domain a spare must stand in; empty for any.

engines.description: The engines it holds spares for, of one shape.

wants.description: How many spares it wants standing.

bearer.description: A Kubernetes token; the cluster's RBAC grants its verbs on the everserve.ai group's resources

clientCertificate.description: A certificate from `everserve-controller certs --operator <name>`, its name one the coordinator's settings make an operator or a viewer
